title: Our world & disclaimer
body:
This wiki explains the difference between the source works that inspired earlier project material and the names and rules used on this website. It is a comparison, not a reproduction of the books or a claim of an official adaptation.

Why the game differs from the books

We deliberately use original public names and an original supporting storyline to reduce reliance on protected fictional expression and reduce confusion about licensing or endorsement. We keep the broad desert science-fiction atmosphere: scarce water, rival houses, dangerous travel and resource trading. The gameplay story does not aim to retell the novels. Separate commemorative banknote artwork includes named Dune characters as unofficial fan interpretations.

Copyright and trademark concerns are part of that editorial decision. They are not a claim that every individual name is copyrighted, or that changing names alone resolves every rights issue. Artwork, detailed fictional expression and branding require separate consideration. Gameplay also differs because it must work with Minecraft, multiplayer balance and the released plugins.

Why our names have a Dutch influence

We chose Dutch-inspired names as a nod to the linguistic texture of Dune. The books use Landsraad, a name with a familiar Dutch form: land and raad, meaning council. A linguistic study of science-fiction word-building discusses that Dutch raad connection. Related forms also occur in other Germanic languages, including Scandinavian languages; we are not claiming that the term, or the books as a whole, originated exclusively in Dutch.

That connection inspired our own approach: names that suggest desert trade, water stewardship, travel and imperial institutions through Dutch sounds and word-building. This is an aesthetic choice for our fan setting, not a claim that our invented houses, planets or organisations are translations of the novels or officially approved replacements.

We draw on Dutch language and word-building to give our desert worlds an original identity: ideas of travel, circles of cooperation, water stewardship and trade inform names such as Vaerkring, Welvaarders and Koopkring. House Aerdrecht, House Harkveen, House Korenholt, House Oordwijk and the Vrijduin continue that direction. Arrakduin combines the Arrak- root with duin; Kaladam keeps the Kala- sound and adds dam; Giedermark keeps Gied- with mark; Kaiterhof retains Kait- with hof; and Sigmadraken IV preserves Sigma and the numbered-world form while echoing Dutch draken. These are invented setting names, not claims of historical Dutch institutions or book-accurate translations.

A broad linguistic influence can inspire new work. Our aim is to create our own names and expression rather than reproduce the source works. Changing a name does not, by itself, clear copyright, trademark or other rights in artwork, stories, characters, branding or adaptations. Neither this explanation nor the unofficial-project disclaimer represents a licence or rights-holder approval. We retain Landsraad as the requested label for the imperial spice and water appointments; it is not presented as an original coinage.

Source terminology and our game labels

The left column identifies terminology in earlier project materials for comparison only. These are not claims that all the listed words are separately protected, or that every term comes from the books.

Our own supporting story

Tavren Sile is a freight surveyor, Mira Vesk coordinates water deliveries, and Archivist Elian Voss preserves cargo records. Their dispute concerns a missing allocation and contradictory receipts. They are unrelated adults whose choices and evidence drive the story. This is an original supporting outline, not a claim that a playable questline has already shipped.

Website names and existing server commands

The public website labels have changed. Existing plugin filenames, world IDs, command arguments and saved data can still use older technical identifiers. Use commands exactly as shown in the field manual. A website rename does not rename a saved Minecraft world or change faction abilities. Older PDF downloads and plugin releases may also use earlier terminology.

Continue to the gameplay manual →

Commemorative note artwork

The Vaerkring Reserve notes feature Minecraft-style fan interpretations of Stilgar, Aliah, Ghanima and Leto, alongside original character Mira Vesk. The 5,000-Dunemark victory scene is imagined game artwork, not a book-accurate event. These character editions reintroduce source-work references; Dutch-inspired names, an original imperial seal and a disclaimer do not provide a licence for those characters or adaptations. The artwork is decorative game-currency art with no cash value and is not offered here as licensed merchandise.

Sources and rights

The official Dune book overview describes the novel’s desert setting and spice premise. For the legal distinction between names and protected expression, see the U.S. Copyright Office guide to material not protected by copyright and its guide to derivative works. Names may separately raise trademark confusion concerns. These U.S. summaries are background, not a worldwide legal clearance.

This project remains unofficial. Original labels do not imply permission from any rights holder. Contact the operators about support or rights concerns at .

title: What is included
body:
The illustrated PDF documents the base gameplay release, DuneCore 1.0.8. This website also includes the optional DiscordSRV feed bridge in DuneCore 1.0.9; see its dedicated integration chapter.

This edition documents the current dunerealms.com release: DuneCore 1.0.8, DuneNPC 1.0.0, DuneTerrain 1.0.7 and DuneEss 1.0.1. It includes the complete Arrakduin guide, operator scepter and admin menus, roaming smugglers, lore-based delivery missions, Imperial spice-sale bonuses, temporary quest camps and real-time deadlines.

ComponentWhat it provides
DuneCoreFactions, reclaimer suits, sandworms, spice harvesting, sun exposure, water trade, politics, KOOPKRING/exchange jobs, admin scepter and Compact sightings.
DuneNPCCompact Routekeepers, Arrakduin smugglers, NPC management GUI, delivery missions, 30-minute deadlines, stationary camps, temporary lights and status particles.
DuneTerrainPlanet generation, safe spawn, Arrakduin formations, deposits, blooms and cave rockhavens. NPC creation now belongs to DuneNPC.
DuneEssDunemarks through Vault, normal spice sales, Compact travel, paged help, landmark teleports and admin bloom placement.
Resource packDesert Sniffer skin, haunted Vrijduin zombies, spice-gold suspicious sand and desert-robed wandering traders.

Reading this edition

Prices and adjustable settings are shipped defaults. The smuggler mission limit is fixed at 30 real minutes. Artwork presents the theme; buildings, clothing detail and dramatic scenery in concept illustrations are not additional released structures or a replacement client pack.

The four non-Arrakduin chapters reserve space for future local gameplay while documenting their current terrain profiles. Arrakduin has the full gameplay guide, not a placeholder.

Verification

The source release is commit a4bb6c9 on main. Builds and 15 automated tests passed across the changed modules. Live Paper/Velocity navigation, lighting, appearance and network behavior still need validation on the deployed server. This manual was checked against the current source and its configuration files.

title: Your first session
body:
1. Open the guide and choose a faction

Use /dune help for the paged chat guide, or /duneess help menu for its inventory version. /dune opens the Dune Routekeeper. A tagged Nether Star is supplied after joining; left- or right-click it to reopen the Routekeeper. /dune menuitem restores the item if you no longer have it.

Choose with /dune choose fremen, or substitute harkonnen, corrino, atreides or ordos. This records your faction, creates an economy account, supplies a kit and requests a free first arrival at your faction homeworld. A normal player cannot change an existing selection; an administrator with dune.admin can.

2. Equip the actual reclaimer suit

The kit is placed in your inventory, not automatically equipped. Wear all four tagged armor pieces. Ordinary leather armor, dyed armor or items renamed at an anvil are not substitutes. A complete reclaimer suit protects against the plugin's Arrakduin heatstroke timer. Matching faction tags are also required for full-set bonuses.

3. Gather supplies and earn Dunemarks

Use the tagged netherite Spice Harvest Shovel on Arrakduin suspicious sand. Pick up the Spice drops and sell with /duneess sell. Cave rockhaven caches also contain tagged spice, food and building materials. Check your balance with /duneess balance before requesting paid Compact travel.

A practical first expedition

Bring the shovel, a complete suit, food and a weapon. Locate shelter before taking on a worm. A default account begins at zero Dunemarks, so ordinary travel initially requires earnings or an admin grant. An unpaid KOOPKRING contract can be accepted without a fare, but you still need a route to Arrakduin and time to meet its quota.

title: Menus and help
body:
The Routekeeper is a configurable chest-style interface. Background colors reflect your faction. Buttons are actions, not free inventory items: clicking them opens a page or runs a player command. Menus expose the same systems available through chat.

Player Spice ExchangeOpen shortcuts to post or cancel a listing, or leave a job.
Wallet / Sell SpiceRead the balance or sell tagged spice through DuneEss.
Reclaimer suit KitReceive another faction kit through /dune kit.
Winged Reclaimer suit UpgradeRun the paid Elytra merge.
Choose FactionOpen the five playable faction selections.

Other ways to navigate

/dune menu and /dune gui also open the Routekeeper. /dune exchange opens the exchange menu; /dune job prints the actual listings and remaining quotas. Interacting with a tagged Vaerkring Routekeeper opens DuneEss's travel menu. The automatically generated Routekeeper is an invulnerable, stationary villager at planet spawn.

Current menu details

The default DuneCore travel page displays only four destinations because its dynamic list is capped at four. Sigmadraken IV is still available through /duneess travel sigma_draconis_iv or the DuneEss travel menu, which lists all five worlds. The exchange page has listing-management shortcuts but no dynamic listing browser; use /dune job to find a sponsor.

Help supports /duneess help <page>, next, previous and menu. The chat guide includes clickable navigation. Some introductory messages and older files omit Oordwijk, but it is a distinct playable faction in the current code.

title: Factions and homeworlds
body:
FactionHomeworldImplemented traits
VrijduinArrakduinTwo spice units per harvested deposit; brief Resistance I refreshes while moving on Arrakduin. Kit has Unbreaking III and leggings with Swift Sneak III.
HarkveenGiedermarkPlayer-caused combat damage is multiplied by 1.15. A matching full reclaimer suit refreshes Strength II.
KorenholtKaiterhofIncoming combat damage from an entity is multiplied by 0.85. Kit armor has Protection III. This does not reduce every environmental damage type.
AerdrechtKaladamMovement events periodically refresh Speed I. A matching full reclaimer suit adds eight health points, equivalent to four hearts.
OordwijkSigmadraken IVA matching suit enables five-second Shadow Step on main-hand Ender Pearl use. Kit includes a replenishing explosive wind charge.

Faction passives use the recorded faction. Full-set effects additionally check that all four equipped pieces are tagged reclaimer suits belonging to your recorded faction. A mixed set can protect against sun exposure if every piece is tagged as a reclaimer suit, but does not grant a faction set bonus.

Arrival and respawning

Faction selection requests travel to the corresponding homeworld without a normal paid fare. On a proxy network, this is a server-transfer request. On a single backend, the homeworld must already be loaded for a local arrival. Respawn is redirected to the homeworld only when that world is loaded on the current backend; there is no general cross-server respawn router.

Choosing carefully

Vrijduin suits favor harvesting and sneaking; Harkveen and Korenholt favor combat; Aerdrecht favor speed and extra full-set health; Oordwijk favor short concealment and explosives. Vaerkring has appearance-related support but is not one of the five player-selectable factions.

title: Reclaimer suits, flight and Oordwijk equipment
body:
Armor that looks like leather but protects like netherite

Faction kits use colored leather reclaimer suits with custom armor attributes. Helmet, chest, legs and boots provide 3, 8, 6 and 3 armor points respectively. Each piece adds three armor toughness and 0.1 knockback resistance. Faction trim patterns distinguish the suits; ordinary armor does not acquire these properties by matching its color.

/dune kit requires a faction and adds another shovel and four armor pieces. The shovel is a tagged netherite shovel with Efficiency V and Unbreaking III. Kits do not include a general food allowance or a conventional melee weapon; rockhaven caches provide food, while weapons must be obtained separately.

Winged reclaimer suit

To use /dune elytra, wear your faction's leather reclaimer suit chestplate, carry an Elytra in storage inventory and have 1,000,000 Dunemarks. The command consumes the carried Elytra, replaces the worn chestplate with a tagged winged Elytra and charges the price. The new item retains custom chest armor protection and faction identity, and qualifies as the reclaimer suit chest slot for heat protection and set bonuses. It is a purpose-built upgrade, not a general enchantment transfer service.

Oordwijk Shadow Step and charge

With a matching full Oordwijk suit, using an Ender Pearl in the main hand grants five seconds of invisibility. The plugin temporarily stores and removes armor, then restores it, returning displaced pieces to inventory or dropping overflow. During removal you do not count as wearing a complete suit, including for sun protection.

The tagged Oordwijk Implosion Charge launches a wind charge and supplies a replacement one tick later. Its impact produces immediate primed TNT attributed to the shooter. Despite its name, it uses ordinary TNT explosion behavior; treat it as destructive explosives rather than a harmless movement tool.

title: Dunemarks, spice sales and Compact travel
body:
VAERKRING RESERVE

The Dunemark collection

Five denominations, five distinctive designs. Parchment, deep teal and imperial gold connect the series; each note has its own Minecraft-style portrait, reverse scene and colour accents. The original crown, sun and dunes seal appears on every denomination.

1 Dunemarks · 5 Dunemarks · 100 Dunemarks · 1,000 Dunemarks · 5,000 Dunemarks

0 Dunemarks · In the search for Leto II

A separate commemorative design. Not an in-game denomination, item, reward or redeemable note.

These are decorative game-currency designs with no cash value. They do not grant a balance, function as bearer tokens or replace the server’s currency ledger. The character editions are unofficial Dune fan artwork; the 5,000 scene is an imagined game interpretation, not a claim of book accuracy. No merchandise licence or rights-holder approval is implied.

Download the original imperial seal → · Java GUI resource pack →

Dunemarks is the currency supplied by DuneEss through Vault. The default spice price is 15 Dunemarks per unit, normal Compact fare is 100 and starting balance is zero. Balances can be negative by default, allowing contract fines to create debt. There are no player-to-player pay or general bank commands in this plugin's command set.

Selling spice

/duneess sell sells all correctly tagged spice in storage inventory. It does not sell ordinary orange dye or an item renamed Spice. With DuneCore enabled, a Vaerkring Trust levy is taken and unauthorized spice sales can create smuggling bounties. A sale of 100 spice has a gross value of 1,500 Dunemarks; the default 1.21% levy rounds up to 19, leaving 1,481 Dunemarks for a player without an appointment. Members of the current Specerhuis or Welvaart House instead receive +33% gross: 1,995 gross, levy 25, net 1,970. See Imperial spice profit and mission eligibility for the complete rules.

Travelling

/duneess travel opens the five-world menu. /duneess travel arrakis requests a specific destination; use the internal world IDs listed in this book. If the destination is the local loaded world, you teleport to its spawn. If networking is enabled and the destination is remote, DuneEss asks the proxy to switch servers.

The appointed Specerhuis faction has free Arrakduin travel. Other travelers normally pay the fare. A local failed teleport refunds the fare; a proxy request refunds only when sending the request itself fails. title: The Arrakduin landscape
body:
Arrakduin is fully implemented in this manual. Its world ID is arrakis. The terrain profile uses Desert biome, sand at the surface and red sand filler. Default base height is 70, height variation 11 and noise scale 0.02. It contains sparse ores, procedural dunes and Dune-specific landmarks, rather than a custom city map.

Landmark or resourceShipped generation setting
Cave rockhavensAbout one anchor per 2,000-block spacing cell.
Untriggered spice bloomsAbout one anchor per 2,000-block spacing cell, where suitable sand is available.
Darkstone formations750-block spacing, 45-55-block radius; about 90-110 blocks across, up to three plateaus.
Oasis trees300-block spacing; default trunk height seven.
Ordinary spice depositsTwo placement attempts per chunk.
Rich random spice patches35% chance per 600-block region; radius 12; target base value 5,000 Dunemarks.

The three-level formations

DuneTerrain 1.0.7 upgrades the old default 10/18 radii to 45/55 automatically on enable, while preserving customized sizes. Darkstone formations use blackstone, basalt and polished blackstone with sand-topped flat terraces. Each formation deterministically chooses one to three nested levels. Height differences between levels are capped at five blocks. The configured default maximum rise of 14 can reduce intervals; a three-level formation can therefore use four-block steps rather than exceeding the total rise.

Trees have persistent leaves, and vanilla vegetation is disabled for Arrakduin. The plugin places a protected Compact Routekeeper at a safe spawn location. Sparse Arrakduin ore attempts include coal, iron and copper between Y -48 and 48, with default vein size five.

Existing terrain is preserved

Generation changes apply to newly generated chunks. Old chunks do not grow additional plateaus after an upgrade. Administrators must plan exploration into new terrain or a backed-up world regeneration if they want the new formations everywhere.

title: Harvesting spice
body:
Suspicious sand on Arrakduin is treated as a spice deposit. With the resource pack it appears bright spice-gold. Harvest it by breaking the block with the tagged Spice Harvest Shovel from your faction kit. A regular netherite shovel is rejected even if it has the same enchantments or name. Other worlds' suspicious sand does not use this Arrakduin harvesting rule.

Yield and provenance

Vrijduin harvest two tagged spice units per deposit; other factions normally get one. Outside an active player-sponsored job, the block drops Spice, represented by tagged orange dye. Its lore records the miner, faction and the current unit price. Collect the drop before using /duneess sell.

Deposits earned from a player job are sold immediately and paid through the contract split, so they do not also drop a second spice item. If a Vrijduin's two-unit yield exceeds the final remaining contract quota by one, the extra unit can still drop as personal spice. Every successful harvest also advances an active KOOPKRING quota.

Respawn behavior

The default regeneration delay is 120 seconds. At the end of that scheduled delay, the location becomes suspicious sand only if its chunk is loaded and the block is air. A replacement block prevents regeneration. There is no retry when the chunk is unloaded, and the scheduled delay is not a persistent offline timer across server restarts.

Estimating value

Values advertised for a field are based on ordinary one-unit harvest at the configured spice price. Actual returns depend on how much sand was converted, how many deposits remain, faction yield, contract assignment and levies. A target field worth 15,000 Dunemarks at a 15-Dunemarks unit price seeks 1,000 deposits; it is not a guaranteed cash reward on discovery.

title: Spice blooms and spice blows
body:
An untriggered generated spice bloom is marked by a 3-by-3 magma patch with a raised central magma block. The server announces its coordinates when the marker's chunk loads. Finding the marker is separate from activating its rich field.

Triggering a blow

A player or other moving living entity touching the marker can trigger it. An arrow or trident impact at the marker also works. The trigger removes the lower magma patch, turns the raised center to glowstone and produces an explosion sound and particle. The source does not use a destructive world explosion for this bloom effect.

Nearby sandy surface blocks within the default 24-block radius become suspicious sand. The target is 15,000 Dunemarks of deposits, using DuneEss's spice price when available. Insufficient sand means fewer deposits. The announcement service identifies a bloom by its marker coordinates, so detonating a previously announced marker does not restart its existing fifteen-minute window.

Admin placement

/duneess admin spicebloom [player] searches for a clear sandy patch about 50 blocks ahead of the selected online player. The player must be on the loaded Arrakduin world. It places an untriggered magma marker and announces it. The command does not instantly harvest the field or place a worm.

Two other types of rich field

Random suspicious-sand patches have their own procedural setting and a 5,000-Dunemarks default target. Defeating a sandworm creates a much larger field targeting 100,000 Dunemarks. The loaded-marker announcement is specifically for spice blooms, not an alert for every ordinary suspicious-sand deposit or random patch in the world.

title: Rockhavens and personal caches
body:
Procedural cave rockhavens have a broad stone-arched entrance, sleeping and kitchen spaces, a winding descent, and a lower reservoir with a waterfall. Their default anchor spacing is 2,000 blocks. Landmarks are generated only where the terrain and region permit placement.

What is in a cache

SupplyAmount and properties
Tagged spice250 units: three stacks of 64 and one stack of 58.
Gold armorHelmet, chestplate, leggings and boots with Protection II and Unbreaking II.
Oak planks32 blocks.
Bread16 items.

Each marked cache is personal to a player. Right-clicking opens a separate cache inventory; taking another player's share does not exhaust yours. Clicking a cache item moves it into your storage inventory, leaving any portion that does not fit. Dragging into the cache is blocked.

Closing the cache

Closing the cache automatically transfers its remaining contents to your inventory and drops any overflow at your location. The player is then marked as having claimed that rockhaven. You cannot repeatedly reopen the same cache for another reward. Make room before opening, and check the ground after closing if your inventory was full.

The cache's gold armor is useful loot, but it is not tagged as a reclaimer suit. Wearing it does not satisfy the Arrakduin heat-protection or faction full-set requirements. Its spice is correctly tagged and can be sold, but claiming a chest is not harvesting deposits and does not advance KOOPKRING's harvested-spice counter.

At the default sale price, 250 cache spice has 3,750 Dunemarks gross value. With the normal Trust levy, the direct sale leaves 3,704 Dunemarks, before any separate consequences of unauthorized trade.

title: Sun exposure and shelter
body:
Arrakduin has a dedicated heatstroke timer. Default lethal exposure is 300 seconds: five minutes of uninterrupted qualifying sunlight. The plugin checks once each second and warns on the first exposed second and at thirty-second intervals.

When the timer runs

All of these conditions must apply: you are alive on Arrakduin, outside Creative and Spectator modes, not wearing a full tagged reclaimer suit, in clear weather, during daytime before world time 12300, and exposed at the top of the surface rather than beneath shelter.

The plugin shows a burning effect while exposure accumulates. Fire-tick damage caused by that active exposure effect is cancelled until the timer expires. At the lethal threshold, the plugin sets health to zero. Ordinary fire, lava and other hazards are separate; a reclaimer suit is not general fire immunity.

What resets exposure

Taking cover, wearing a full tagged suit, reaching night or otherwise ceasing to meet the exposure conditions resets the timer. You do not need to wait for gradual recovery. The stored exposure entry is removed and the associated fire effect cleared.

Arrakduin defaults to persistent daytime

DuneTerrain disables the daylight cycle on Arrakduin and sets world time to 6000 during setup. Under that default, waiting for a natural sunset is not a reliable survival plan. Use a suit or reach shelter. An operator can alter world time or game rules separately.

Equipment edge cases

A winged reclaimer suit counts as the chest piece. A mixed-faction set can still satisfy heat protection if every equipped slot has the reclaimer suit tag, but faction set bonuses require matching tags. Oordwijk Shadow Step temporarily removes armor, so its five-second concealment also temporarily breaks the full reclaimer suit condition.

title: Dune Maw: model, AI and combat
body:
The current sandworm uses a real Sniffer as the visible, damageable body. An invisible Husk supplies native zombie-family targeting, pursuit and melee attacks. The body follows its controller each server tick. It is a composite gameplay creature: a vanilla Sniffer silhouette with a desert worm skin, not a custom elongated sandworm mesh.

Sandworm propertyDefault
Visible bodyAdult Sniffer; scale 3.5; 500 health points.
Hostile controllerInvisible adult Husk; melee damage attribute 8; movement attribute 0.33.
Automatic population capThree visible sandworms in Arrakduin.
Automatic successful-spawn interval3,600 seconds, saved in config.
Spawn chance35% per eligible player check when the cooldown permits.
Check frequencyEvery ten seconds, after the initial scheduled delay.

Encounter rules

Natural spawns require Arrakduin and a sandy surface near a player. The chosen location is about 22-40 blocks away; a worm already within the nearby-entity check can prevent another spawn for that player. The hour-long cooldown starts after a successful automatic spawn, not merely after an unsuccessful check.

The visible Sniffer can be attacked and killed. Damage to the hidden controller is cancelled, so it does not become a second reward-bearing enemy. The controller handles melee targeting; combat damage received depends on ordinary combat rules and applicable faction defenses. The worm's spawn produces cloud particles and a Warden roar.

Persistence and conversion

Both parts carry saved partner UUIDs. Existing loaded Husk-based worms from 1.0.4 are converted to the visible Sniffer implementation without resetting their remaining health. The plugin repairs links after load and removes the counterpart when a linked entity dies. Live-server movement and collision behavior still need testing on the deployed Paper build.

title: Defeating and summoning a sandworm
body:
Death rewards

Killing the tagged visible body removes the invisible controller. The worm has no normal item drops or experience reward. Instead, it strikes a visual lightning effect and converts available sandy terrain around the death location into suspicious-sand deposits.

The field targets 100,000 Dunemarks at ordinary base yield. At 15 Dunemarks per unit this means a target of 6,667 deposits. Its radius is derived from the target, and each eligible position also has an 85% placement chance. Unsuitable terrain can reduce actual deposit count. The death message reports how much was actually placed; it does not deposit 100,000 Dunemarks into the killer's account.

If at least one deposit is placed, this new spice field receives an Arrakduin coordinates warning and its own fifteen-minute Compact countdown. Harvest it using the same tagged shovel and contract rules as any other Arrakduin deposit.

Admin summon command

/dune summon sandworm summons at the executing player's current position on Arrakduin. /dune summon sandworm 120 76 -240 summons at explicit absolute X/Y/Z coordinates in the loaded Arrakduin world. Console can use the coordinate form, without a leading slash in the console input.

Both forms require dune.admin, granted to operators by default. Coordinates must be finite numbers within the world border and build height, with open feet and head space. The coordinate-free form fails outside Arrakduin. A server without a loaded Arrakduin world cannot summon there.

Admin summons bypass the automatic population cap and do not alter the saved automatic cooldown. They use the same Sniffer body, zombie AI, configured attributes, sighting messages and death-field behavior as natural worms. Summoning can therefore deliberately create more than the default three-worm population.

title: Haunted Vrijduin and rich-field danger
body:
Haunted Vrijduin are hostile zombie raiders, distinct from sandworms and from water-retaliation Angry Locals. They spawn on Arrakduin near players and are more likely near high-value suspicious-sand fields. The resource pack gives zombies their haunted Vrijduin appearance.

Raider propertyDefault
Population cap12 tagged raiders on Arrakduin.
Regular chance per player check8%.
Chance near a rich field45%.
Rich-field search32-block radius; more than 5,000 Dunemarks of remaining base-value deposits.
Health / attack attribute36 health points / 6 attack damage.
Movement attribute0.28.
GearIron sword and leather helmet, both with zero gear drop chance.

How a raider appears

Checks run every ten seconds. A nearby tagged raider within the local-entity check prevents another for that player. The spawner tries sandy positions roughly 16-32 blocks away with clear feet and head space, then targets the player. These are configured probability checks, not a promise that a raider appears after a fixed time.

Raider sunlight combustion is cancelled by the plugin. Their equipment is for behavior and appearance, not a dependable source of an iron sword. They may despawn when far away. Unlike sandworms, their death does not run the special worm spice-field reward.

title: The fifteen-minute Compact notice
body:
Session 2 introduces a discovery window for sandworms and spice blooms. The first message is local to the Arrakduin server, includes X/Y/Z and warns that the Vaerkring will notify other worlds in fifteen minutes.

Which events create sightings

A generated, untriggered bloom marker is found when its chunk loads, including loaded chunks checked at server startup.

An admin places a bloom marker; a previously unannounced marker erupts.

A sandworm spawns or loads, including admin summons.

A defeated sandworm produces a new field with at least one spice deposit.

Countdown and global delivery

At the saved deadline, DuneCore sends a lore announcement through the proxy's standard BungeeCord Message channel to ALL online players. The Compact message includes the recorded sighting coordinates. With network.enabled: false, delivery is local instead.

The deadline uses elapsed real time, not a fifteen-minute Minecraft day. The service saves timers and identities in plugins/DuneCore/arrakis-announcements.yml. Restarting preserves the original deadline. Chunk reloads do not restart a countdown for the same bloom coordinates or worm UUID.

Plugin messaging requires an online player connection on the sending backend. If Arrakduin is empty when the notice is due, it remains pending until a carrier is available. The standard channel has no delivery acknowledgment; the plugin records a notice as sent after submitting it, and cannot prove every proxy client received it.

Interpreting coordinates

Coordinates are the initial sighting, not a live moving-worm tracker. A worm may move, despawn or die before the Compact message arrives. The notice also does not reserve the field for the discoverer, lock harvesting, or establish political ownership. The fifteen-minute window is an information embargo.

title: Finite water and selling buckets
body:
Arrakduin water is deliberately constrained. Natural source buckets collected through the water listener receive the Arrakduin Water - Finite Source tag. /dune water sell sells these tagged buckets. Ordinary water buckets bought or collected elsewhere are not automatically accepted as Arrakduin trade goods.

Water flow is cancelled on Arrakduin. Emptying water buckets there is blocked, and the listener prevents new ice or snow formation and water-cauldron filling. The intended loop is to locate existing natural sources, collect finite buckets, and trade them rather than build a renewable placed-water farm. The source-tag check applies to natural water generally; it is not tied to ownership of one specific rockhaven.

Price and legal status

Base price is half the spice price using integer division, with a minimum of one. At the default spice price of 15, base water value is seven Dunemarks per bucket. Members of the appointed Welvaart House receive the legal base price. Others are treated as smugglers and receive a 45% gross premium, rounded over the entire batch. The Trust levy is then taken from gross revenue.

For ten buckets, an authorized sale has gross value 70, levy one and net 69. An unauthorized sale has rounded gross value 102, levy two and net 100. Tagged buckets are removed by the sale; the command does not return empty buckets.

Career commands versus actual authorization

/dune water guild, smuggler and status select or display an in-memory career label. The actual sale rule uses imperial Welvaart House authorization, not that chosen label. Choosing Compact does not make an unappointed faction legal. The label resets on restart.

Unauthorized collection has a default 30% retaliation chance, potentially announcing a local bounty and spawning two Angry Local Husks targeting the collector. The collection retaliation listener currently also lacks an Arrakduin-world guard; administrators should consider this when testing collection on other planets. Shared bounty records require PostgreSQL.

title: Meeting the roaming smugglers
body:
Arrakduin Smugglers use wandering-trader bodies, native AI and the desert smuggler skin. Right-click with your main hand to open the contract menu. They roam toward nearby destinations; up to six are maintained in loaded chunks near players by default, with at most two automatic additions per minute. Their normal despawn delay is 48,000 server ticks; active quest camps suspend that countdown.

Who gets an offer?

Members of the currently appointed Specerhuis or Welvaart House receive no smuggling offers. A smuggler refuses them in dialogue and points them to ordinary spice sales with the 33% Imperial bonus. Other players can accept a spice or water run. Authorization is checked again when accepting and delivering, so an appointment gained during a mission can block completion.

The Unmarked Spice Run64 tagged spice1,392 Dunemarks1,375 Dunemarks
Water for the Hidden Rockhaven4 tagged water buckets41 Dunemarks40 Dunemarks

Rewards equal the cargo's normal base value plus 45%, rounded over the contract, then the Trust levy applies. The reward and cargo requirement are fixed when accepted. Only one smuggler contract may be active per player. These are separate from KOOPKRING quotas and player-sponsored exchange jobs.

Recognizing the trader

title: The Unmarked Spice Run
body:
"Imperial patrols count every grain of spice. Our hidden buyers need a shipment without a seal."

The smuggler asks you to move a cargo of spice beyond the Imperial ledgers. Accept the spice run, gather the required tagged spice, then find another Arrakduin Smuggler at least 64 horizontal blocks from the departure point. Return to your original contact is not a valid delivery.

Accept, carry, deliver

Right-click an eligible smuggler and select The Unmarked Spice Run.

Carry 64 tagged Spice by default. Ordinary orange dye and renamed items are not accepted. Tagged cache spice also qualifies; the mission checks carried cargo, not newly harvested quota progress.

Reach a different smuggler, at least 64 blocks from the stored starting X/Z. Right-click, then select the active delivery chest in the contract menu.

Stay within eight blocks while the action executes. The receiving NPC must still exist on Arrakduin and you must still be eligible.

Only the required amount is consumed. Extra spice stays in your inventory. A successful default run pays 1,375 Dunemarks after the 17-Dunemarks Trust levy. The existing smuggling-bounty system is called using gross reward; shared tracking requires PostgreSQL.

A short window

You have 30 real minutes from acceptance, including offline time and server downtime. The menu and /dune smuggle status show remaining time, required cargo, reward and departure coordinates. Completing after the deadline is rejected. Cancellation or expiry keeps cargo and pays no reward; there is no smuggler failure fine.

On delivery: "No seal, no names. The spice is already on its way. The Emperor's men may have noticed you."

title: Water for the Hidden Rockhaven
body:
"A rockhaven beyond the patrol routes is running dry. Carry its water quietly. On Arrakduin, water is life."

This run carries finite-source Arrakduin water to a distant contact who supplies a hidden rockhaven. The narrative does not place a new rockhaven structure or assign a fixed cave destination: delivery is to another valid smuggler.

Cargo and route

Accept the water run, then carry four tagged Arrakduin Water - Finite Source buckets by default. Ordinary water buckets do not qualify. Deliver through the active contract chest to a different smuggler at least 64 horizontal blocks from your departure point, within the 30-minute real-time window.

At the default spice price of 15 Dunemarks, the water base is seven per bucket. Four buckets at the 45% smuggling premium give rounded gross reward 41; the levy is one, leaving 40 Dunemarks. The mission consumes only the required water buckets and returns empty buckets. If the empties cannot fit, they drop near the player.

How this differs from selling water

/dune water sell sells all tagged water in your inventory and does not return empty buckets. The smuggler mission is a timed delivery with a locked reward and a different NPC destination. Water-collection retaliation and the finite-water rules still apply while gathering cargo. Mission completion also invokes the shared bounty system.

Landsraad appointments block smuggler missions regardless of the selected water-career label. An appointment acquired mid-run blocks delivery; /dune smuggle cancel remains available. No cargo is taken when a mission is cancelled or expires.

On delivery: "Tonight the rockhaven drinks. Keep your route secret; the water monopoly has long eyes."

title: Lights, particles and the 30-minute limit
body:
The smuggler who issued your active mission becomes a quest contact. It stops moving, loses collision and gravity, becomes invulnerable and cannot naturally despawn. Invisible level-15 light blocks brighten its surroundings. The destination remains any different valid smuggler along the required route.

StateVisible signalNPC and camp behavior
No open contractGreen dustNormal roaming; no temporary camp lights.
One or more open contractsPurple dustSource NPC stationary and protected; temporary illumination active.
Last contract endsReturns to greenPrevious AI, gravity, collision, vulnerability and despawn timer restored; lights removed.

The deadline uses the real clock

Each accepted contract stores an absolute deadline 30 minutes ahead. Logging out, unloading chunks, restarting or stopping the server does not pause it. Expiry is processed when the running plugin checks its saved state; a server that was offline applies overdue expiry after startup. The clock shown in a menu is a snapshot; reopen it or use status for an updated reading.

"The patrols have changed. Your 30-minute window is gone." Expired missions pay nothing and consume no cargo. There is no fine. A camp stays active if another player's contract from the same NPC is still open; it clears after that last contract completes, is cancelled or expires.

Terrain and recovery

The plugin plans up to five invisible lights around the source contact, placing them only in empty blocks in loaded chunks. Existing terrain and existing light blocks are preserved. Overlapping camps share ownership. Original block data is journaled before placement; completion removes owned lights and keeps unrelated replacement blocks intact.

Cleanup does not force-load chunks. If a camp is unloaded when a quest ends, normal state is restored when it becomes available. A normal shutdown clears loaded camps; outstanding contracts reactivate on startup. Green/purple particles update about once per second.

title: KOOPKRING hourly contracts
body:
KOOPKRING jobs are server-issued quota contracts, separate from player-sponsored exchange jobs. /dune serverjobs lists the current offers. /dune serverjobs accept small-spice-run accepts a current template. The Routekeeper also has a KOOPKRING menu with an active-contract summary.

Contract IDQuota / pay / limitFailure fine
small-spice-run100 spice / 3,000 Dunemarks / 30 min150 Dunemarks
Compact-supply250 spice / 8,500 Dunemarks / 45 min425 Dunemarks
imperial-contract500 spice / 20,000 Dunemarks / 60 min1,000 Dunemarks
dangerous-harvest800 spice / 35,000 Dunemarks / 90 min1,750 Dunemarks

Three shuffled offers are normally available each hour. The rotation follows UTC epoch hour boundaries, rather than counting sixty minutes from your last acceptance. Accepting is free, starts the template's own time limit and permits only one active KOOPKRING contract per player.

Completing and failing

Successfully harvesting Arrakduin deposits advances the quota by yielded units, including the Vrijduin two-unit yield. Selling carried spice or taking cache spice does not advance it. Reaching the quota pays the configured amount directly to the wallet. There is no requirement to hand over inventory spice to an NPC.

Failure costs 5% of the offered pay, rounded up. A ten-second check expires contracts even while a player is offline; real time continues through server downtime. With default negative balances enabled, a fine can create debt. An accepted contract retains its ID, progress and original acceptance time in local state. If its template is removed, it disappears without a template-based fine.

An administrator can edit server-jobs.yml and use /dune serverjobs reload. Offers remain limited to the current selection until the next rotation. Reloaded quota, pay and duration values are resolved from the current template, so changes can affect accepted contracts.

title: The player spice exchange
body:
Player jobs split the sale value of newly harvested spice between a worker and sponsor. They are not prepaid procurement orders: the sponsor earns 85% of the harvest's base sale value and the worker earns 15%. Posting does not withdraw an escrow sum from the sponsor.

Posting and accepting

/dune job post 1000 creates your listing with a quota between one and 100,000. You may have one listing at a time. /dune job lists sponsors and remaining quota. /dune job accept PlayerName accepts someone else's open listing; a UUID is also accepted. You cannot take your own listing, take a listing already occupied or accept another while you are already a worker.

Accepting assigns the worker and requests /duneess travel arrakis. The assignment occurs before the travel request; a failed trip does not automatically cancel the assignment. You may need to fund the fare or contact the administrator before travelling manually.

How payment works

Each credited harvested unit is paid immediately. Rounding is based on accumulated listing value, maintaining the 15/85 split across the job. At a 15-Dunemarks unit price, a completed 100-unit listing is worth 1,500: the worker receives 225 and sponsor 1,275. These direct contract payouts do not run the ordinary DuneEss direct-sale levy path.

Harvested job spice is not also dropped for a second sale. KOOPKRING progress is credited as well, so the two job systems can advance from the same successful harvesting action. Any yield above the remaining player-job quota falls back to personal spice.

Leaving, cancellation and saving

/dune job finish leaves your worker assignment; it does not force-complete the quota. /dune job cancel cancels your own unclaimed listing, but refuses while a worker is assigned. Listings are local to a backend. Worker assignments are in memory and need reacceptance after restart. In shared-database mode, the current save path returns after saving player profiles and does not persist new exchange-listing changes, so do not rely on listing restart durability in that mode.

title: Politics, elections and the Vaerkring Trust
body:
/dune politics and /dune trust access the same prototype political system. /dune politics status shows the Trust balance, election bucket, faction, leader, Emperor, stored appointments and invasion state. You need a selected faction for actions other than status.

The treasury and elections

The default Trust levy is 1.21% of applicable gross direct sales, rounded up. /dune politics deposit 500 voluntarily withdraws 500 from your wallet and adds it to the Trust if you have sufficient funds. The Trust is not a personal withdrawable bank account.

Use /dune politics vote PlayerName for your faction leader and emperorvote PlayerName for the Emperor. A candidate must be online and have a playable faction. Faction-leader candidates must belong to your house; imperial candidates may come from another house. Each player can cast one ballot in each applicable election bucket. The current highest tally determines the winner immediately, with lexicographic UUID tie-breaking.

Election buckets are seven-day Unix epoch divisions, not a scheduled election ceremony at a local Monday midnight. Leaders and the Emperor are recalculated from the current bucket's ballots. There is no separate close-election or campaign system.

Invasions

The current elected faction leader can use /dune politics invasion <house> to target a different playable faction. Default cost is 50,000 from the Trust, duration sixty minutes and required defense contributions five. Only one unexpired invasion is allowed.

Members of the defending house contribute using /dune politics defend; each stored defender identity contributes once. Reaching five broadcasts that the invasion was repelled and clears its active deadline. This is a ledger-and-announcement prototype: there is no automatic territory capture, structure destruction, NPC army or attacker victory payout when time expires. Status can retain stored attacker and defender labels after expiry. Shared politics storage remains a whole-record prototype, not fully transactional multi-server governance.

BY APPOINTMENT OF THE EMPEROR

Landsraad appointments

The Emperor appoints a spice-trading house to the Specerhuis office and a water-selling house to the Welvaart House office. These are the Landsraad appointments. The ceremonial artwork represents the offices; it does not confirm that either office is currently occupied.

title: Imperial rights, permits and bounties
body:
The Emperor's appointments

The current elected Emperor can appoint a Specerhuis with /dune politics steward <house> and a Welvaart House with /dune politics houseofwater <house>. Each office can be appointed once for the current Emperor and election bucket. The two offices may belong to different playable factions.

Rights depend on the current winning Emperor, matching stored term and appointed house. They can cease when the week changes or the winner changes. Status displays stored appointment labels, which may no longer be legally active. The Specerhuis has free Arrakduin travel; the Welvaart House has authorized water trading. Both current appointed houses get sanctioned normal spice sales with +33% gross before levy, and both are barred from NPC smuggling missions. The present arrival exemption checks the Specerhuis, not both offices.

Arrival permits and trade bounties

The sanctioned travel path can issue a two-minute, single-use PostgreSQL permit. On Arrakduin arrival, a Steward member is exempt; otherwise a valid permit is consumed or the player is marked wanted. Without the shared database, enforcement logs its limitation rather than maintaining shared permits.

Unauthorized spice or water sales can issue a bounty equal to their gross sale value. Unauthorized arrival's default bounty is derived from half the spice price plus the 45% premium, yielding eleven Dunemarks with the default values. Water collection retaliation uses its own base-price calculation. These paths are related but not identical pricing formulas.

title: The Imperial Admin Scepter
body:
Operators automatically receive a glowing, gold-named blaze rod called Imperial Admin Scepter. The supply check runs about every five seconds, covering joins, respawns and players newly opped while online. It does not add another rod when one is already in the player's inventory. A full inventory is retried when a slot becomes free.

Right-click the scepter in your main hand to open Imperial Administration. /dune admin opens the same GUI. /dune adminitem requests recovery of the rod. Its persistent tag identifies it; renaming an ordinary blaze rod does not create an admin item. It currently uses the vanilla blaze-rod appearance with glint and custom model data 1006.

title: NPC migration, settings and recovery
body:
DuneNPC stores configuration and local mission data in plugins/DuneNPC. First installation copies smuggling.yml and smuggler-camps.yml from DuneCore only if the destination is absent. Source files remain as backups. The first DuneNPC config imports legacy smuggler settings and Terrain's Compact NPC enabled flag. Later edits belong in DuneNPC/config.yml.

Setting / fileDefault or purpose
Compact-npc.enabledtrue; automatic Compact Routekeepers at planet spawn.
smugglers.enabledtrue; roaming traders and mission interaction.
smugglers.max-traders6; automatic population in loaded chunks, bounded from 2 to 20.
smugglers.spice-amount64; bounded from 1 to 4,096 on a new offer.
smugglers.water-amount4; bounded from 1 to 36 on a new offer.
smuggling.ymlPlayer UUID, cargo, reward, source NPC, departure X/Z and absolute deadline.
smuggler-camps.ymlOriginal NPC state and owned temporary light blocks for restoration.

Restart and upgrade behavior

The mission limit is fixed at 30 real minutes. Old contracts without deadlines get one initial window during upgrade; saved deadlines never reset on ordinary restart. Local files do not transfer missions between backends. Install the matching Core and Terrain versions so old NPC logic is not running alongside DuneNPC.

Before editing state, stop the server and back up both NPC state files. Do not delete only the light journal while camps are active: it records what needs restoration. Unloaded camp cleanup waits for chunks to become available. Normal shutdown restores loaded camps and the next startup reactivates unexpired contracts.

Diagnosing an NPC issue

If the admin button reports DuneNPC missing, check all dependency JARs and enable logs. A vanilla-looking smuggler needs the current client pack. A refused mission may mean a current Imperial appointment; a refused delivery may mean deadline, cargo tag, same trader, insufficient route distance or distance from the receiver. /dune smuggle cancel lets a player abandon a blocked mission without losing cargo.

title: Installing and upgrading
body:
The release targets Minecraft Java / Paper 1.21.4 and Java 21. Install DuneCore 1.0.8, DuneNPC 1.0.0, DuneTerrain 1.0.7 and DuneEss 1.0.1 alongside Vault. The full GitHub server package includes Vault 2.5.0; the plugin-update ZIP includes the four project plugins and resource pack and expects Vault to be installed already.

Upgrade sequence

Stop the server and back up worlds, plugin folders and shared database state.

Replace the previous Core and Terrain JARs with the matching versions, add DuneNPC, and keep only one JAR per plugin. Retain DuneEss and Vault. Remove obsolete dunerealms.com.jar if present.

Keep existing state files. DuneNPC copies legacy smuggling.yml and smuggler-camps.yml only when its own copies are absent; originals remain as backups.

First-time DuneNPC configuration imports Core's smuggler settings and Terrain's Compact NPC enabled flag. Thereafter edit plugins/DuneNPC/config.yml. Do not run an older Core's NPC logic alongside DuneNPC.

Start and check plugin enable messages. Confirm the planet/proxy settings, open the admin rod's DuneNPC Management page, and test one mission.

Existing NPCs and contracts

Persistent tags are retained, so existing Compact Routekeepers and smugglers are recognized. Legacy undated contracts receive one initial 30-minute window on migration. Contracts with a saved deadline keep it; restarting does not reset the timer. Camp restoration handles loaded chunks and resumes cleanup when unloaded chunks become available.

Resource pack

Enable DuneResourcePack.zip in the client's .minecraft/resourcepacks folder. Vanilla and Fabric use the same pack; it does not belong in mods. Automatic server delivery needs a direct-download resource-pack URL and client acceptance. Reload the updated pack for smuggler robes. Standard packs change all wandering trader textures, although smuggling behavior is Arrakduin-only.

Build from source

Run gradle clean build with Java 21 / Gradle 8.14 in dunerealms.com-minecraft-only, DuneNPC, DuneTerrain and DuneEss. DuneNPC's Gradle build compiles the sibling Core dependency; its JAR contains only NPC classes. Install both Core and NPC on the server. In DuneNPC, gradle build :DuneCore:build also runs Core's tests.

title: World generation and primary-world setup
body:
DuneTerrain selects one planet world per backend from server.planet in its config. Valid values are Arrakduin, giedi_prime, Kaiterhof, Kaladam and sigma_draconis_iv. The world name matches that ID. All profiles remain in the file, but only the selected planet is created by the normal backend setup.

Separate planet world

If Paper's primary world is the ordinary world named world, the plugin creates its selected separate planet after Paper loads its worlds and directly supplies its generator. It also chooses a safe spawn and optionally places the Compact Routekeeper. New players who appear in the primary world are subsequently moved to the configured local planet spawn.

Planet as Paper's primary world

If server.properties level-name is Arrakduin, Paper must know the generator during initial primary-world loading. In bukkit.yml, the worlds.Arrakduin section needs generator DuneTerrain:Arrakduin and biome-provider DuneTerrain:Arrakduin. For another selected planet, use that ID in all corresponding keys and values. Paper's global/world-default behavior files do not select this generator.

Terrain changes and backups

The generator sets biome, height, filler, surface, water, vegetation and ores only during new chunk generation. Existing chunks are retained. If a world was generated with a different generator, changing config will not replace its rivers or hills. DuneTerrain logs a mismatch when it finds a selected world without its generator.

To intentionally regenerate a world, first stop and back up the server and move the specific old world folder aside before creating a fresh world. Never delete a live world's folder. Regeneration resets built structures and world-contained entities; player and plugin state needs separate consideration.

Arrakduin setup freezes the daylight cycle at time 6000. Giedermark starts at 18000; other profiles start at 6000 with a running daylight cycle. Spawn X/Z defaults are zero for all five planets.

title: The five-backend network
body:
The intended topology is one Paper backend per planet behind a Velocity proxy. Each backend has the same project plugins, but a different selected local planet. DuneTerrain server.planet and DuneCore network.local-planet must match. DuneEss uses the DuneCore network settings by default.

Displayed worldPlugin world IDDefault proxy server name
ArrakduinArrakduinArrakduin
Giedermarkgiedi_primegiedi-prime
KaiterhofKaiterhofKaiterhof
KaladamKaladamKaladam
Sigmadraken IVsigma_draconis_ivsigma-draconis-iv

The proxy server name must exactly match its configured name. Underscored world IDs and hyphenated proxy names are different strings. Compact travel uses the BungeeCord Connect channel. Global Compact sightings use Message with recipient ALL; the sending backend needs an online player connection.

Proxy prerequisites

Velocity must have BungeeCord plugin-message compatibility enabled through bungee-plugin-message-channel. Configure matching forwarding on the proxy and each Paper backend, and keep backend ports protected from direct player connections. Follow your installed server version's official setup documentation for exact forwarding fields; the plugin is not a replacement for proxy authentication configuration.

What is not a guaranteed network transfer

Connect is asynchronous with no success acknowledgment. The plugin cannot guarantee a destination is online or refund every failed remote arrival. Homeworld selection requests a transfer, but cross-server respawning needs separate routing. Job offers and exchange listings are backend-local. A GUI may show destinations that are not reachable until the administrator configures them.

Do not interpret the existence of all five terrain profiles as proof all five backend servers are running. The reserved planet pages describe the configured base worlds, not their deployment status.

title: Saving, shared data and recovery
body:
StateCurrent storage and behavior
Faction selection and inventoryLocal faction data in players.yml by default; PostgreSQL player profiles when enabled. Shared inventory is saved on quit/profile saves and loaded on join.
DunemarksDuneEss balances.yml locally; optional shared dune_economy_balances PostgreSQL table.
Politics and Trustpolitics.yml locally or a shared YAML record in dune_politics.
KOOPKRING offers and accepted jobsLocal server-jobs-state.yml, with original acceptance timestamps.
Player exchangeLocal listings in players.yml in local mode; workers in memory. Shared-mode listing persistence is incomplete.
NPC missions / quest campsDuneNPC smuggling.yml and smuggler-camps.yml; local real-time deadlines and restoration records.
Compact sightingsLocal Arrakduin-announcements.yml with deadlines and duplicate identities.
Permits and bountiesPostgreSQL tables; no equivalent shared local-file implementation.
Rockhaven cache claimsPlayer persistent tags for each cache ID. These are not included as a separate shared profile field.

Enabling PostgreSQL

DuneCore config has database.enabled, jdbc-url, username and password. It creates its profile, politics, permit and bounty tables when initialized. If required shared database initialization fails, DuneCore disables rather than starting its gameplay without that connection. DuneEss normally reuses DuneCore's database settings when enabled.

DuneEss maintains a separate shared economy table and can import legacy database or local balances when that table is empty. A shared-economy initialization failure can fall back to its local ledger; inspect logs rather than assuming the whole network still uses one authoritative balance store.

Scope of synchronization

The current profile blob contains inventory and faction. It does not synchronize every aspect of Minecraft player state, every plugin tag or the local job files. Whole-record politics saving and multi-step payments are not fully transactional across simultaneous backends. Back up the database and local files together before changing storage mode. Do not edit runtime state while the plugins are active.

title: Troubleshooting and current limits
body:
SymptomWhat to check
Sandworm still looks like a HuskConfirm DuneCore 1.0.8 is the only installed Core JAR and the world has loaded the converted worm. A skin alone cannot change a Husk into a Sniffer.
Sniffer looks like ordinary green SnifferReplace and enable the updated resource pack; check automatic download caching and client acceptance.
Cannot summonCheck dune.admin, loaded Arrakduin, numeric coordinates, border/build-height and open space. From console include x y z.
Cannot harvest a depositUse the tagged kit shovel, not ordinary netherite or an anvil rename, and ensure you are on Arrakduin.
Burning or heatstrokeEquip all four tagged suit slots or take shelter. Default Arrakduin time does not progress into night.
No Compact global notice at deadlineCheck pending state, a player on Arrakduin, network.enabled and proxy channel compatibility. Restart does not reset the deadline.
Travel unavailable or fare lostCheck proxy names and destination availability; Connect has no arrival acknowledgment.
No new plateaus near spawnExisting chunks retain their earlier generation. Explore new chunks or arrange backed-up regeneration.

Behavior to understand before running a public economy

Water career labels do not determine legal pricing. Smuggling and arrival authorization require correct political state and PostgreSQL for shared enforcement. Operator status is not a substitute for an elected Emperor. KOOPKRING deadlines run through offline time, and fines can create debt. Ordinary deposit respawn delays do not persist through a restart.

The plugin has no dedicated thirst meter, custom worm mesh, built-in cities, territory-capture engine, general bank/pay system or universal multiplayer inventory transaction manager. The Sniffer body follows a hidden vanilla controller, so its collision and appearance should be checked in a live staging environment. These are current implementation boundaries, not features implied by the Dune lore names.

title: Rockhaven cache supplies
body:
Lore passages are creative flavour for dunerealms.com. The mechanical descriptions remain the gameplay reference.

Each unclaimed personal cache contains all six supply types below. Claiming supplies is separate from harvesting a KOOPKRING quota.

Gold helmet

One per personal cache. Protection II and Unbreaking II. Not a tagged reclaimer suit.

Lore A bright relic recovered from a rockhaven cache; its gleam hints at the wealth that crosses Arrakduin.

Gold chestplate

One per personal cache. Protection II and Unbreaking II. Does not prevent heatstroke.

Lore Desert traders prize its shine, though a reclaimer suit remains the wiser companion under a merciless sun.

Gold leggings

One per personal cache. Protection II and Unbreaking II.

Lore A gilded cache find, worn with the memory of older expeditions and fortunes lost in sand.

Gold boots

One per personal cache. Protection II and Unbreaking II.

Lore Their gold catches the desert light, a small extravagance in a world that measures life in water.

Oak planks

32 per cache. Ordinary building supplies.

Lore Shelter begins with simple materials; a wooden brace can turn a hollow in the rock into a refuge.

Bread

16 per cache. Ordinary food. The cache also contains 250 tagged spice units.

Lore A plain ration shared in the shade can matter more to a traveler than a chest of spice.

Cache overflow is transferred or dropped when you close the inventory. Each player can claim a specific rockhaven once. The enchanted gold gear does not qualify as a reclaimer suit.

title: Travel, weapons and explosives
body:
Lore passages are creative flavour for dunerealms.com. The mechanical descriptions remain the gameplay reference.

These ordinary Minecraft items support plugin mechanics. They are not all granted by a faction kit.

Ender Pearl

Main-hand use activates Oordwijk Shadow Step when wearing a matching full set.

Lore For Oordwijk, a brief passage through shadow is another tool in the art of remaining unseen.

Ordinary Elytra

Carry one while wearing a reclaimer suit chestplate for the paid winged upgrade.

Lore Unadapted wings await the craft of a winged reclaimer suit before desert flight can wear a faction’s identity.

Arrow

An arrow impact can activate a magma-marked spice bloom.

Lore A narrow line of intent, pointing toward the next route or the next danger beyond the dunes.

Trident

A trident impact can also trigger a spice bloom.

Lore A weapon whose shape recalls water-rich worlds, brought into a land where water itself is guarded.

TNT

The tagged Oordwijk charge creates an immediate primed TNT explosion on impact.

Lore An explosive answer to stone and opposition, echoing the dangerous tools carried on frontier expeditions.

Iron sword

Haunted Vrijduin raiders carry one. Their equipment has zero gear drop chance.

Lore A familiar blade in unfamiliar sands; allegiance gives its bearer a cause, but not immunity.

title: Markers and supporting items
body:
Lore passages are creative flavour for dunerealms.com. The mechanical descriptions remain the gameplay reference.

Recognize the equipment and landscape markers involved in Arrakduin gameplay and navigation.

Raider leather helmet

Ordinary helmet worn by Haunted Vrijduin raiders. Not faction-tagged loot.

Lore A raider’s worn hood carries the dust of harsh roads and the suspicion of desert travelers.

Empty bucket

Used for natural-source collection. Normal water sales remove buckets; NPC water missions return empties.

Lore An empty vessel on Arrakduin is a question: where will the next precious measure of water be found?

Suspicious sand

Arrakduin spice deposit. The resource pack makes it spice-gold; harvest with the tagged shovel.

Lore An unremarkable patch may conceal the memory of a spicebloom beneath its surface.

Magma marker

Untriggered bloom: 3x3 lower patch with a raised central magma block.

Lore A hot signal beneath the sand gives the spicebloom its visual language of pressure and eruption.

Glowstone marker

Raised bloom center after eruption. Nearby suitable sand becomes spice deposits.

Lore A light in the stone suggests a hidden cache, a promise of supplies beyond the reach of the sun.

Compact compass

A Routekeeper interface icon for travel. It is a menu symbol, not a separately granted travel artifact.

Lore A celestial pointer for those who trust their destination to routes charted beyond the desert horizon.

title: Website and DiscordSRV feeds
search: website DiscordSRV Discord exchange news API notifications buy sell offers
body:
The website includes a searchable manual, Races & Houses, Exchange and News. The optional DuneCore 1.0.9 bridge publishes public game notifications and read-only Arrakduin market snapshots through DiscordSRV. The bridge is disabled by default.

Connecting the Minecraft server

Install DiscordSRV and DuneCore 1.0.9. In plugins/DuneCore/config.yml set website.discord.enabled to true, website.discord.exchange-channel-id to the dedicated market channel ID and website.discord.news-channel-id to the dedicated public-news channel ID. Restart after editing. Configure news on each backend; only Arrakduin publishes the exchange.

Connecting the website reader

Configure DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN, DISCORD_PUBLISHER_ID, DISCORD_EXCHANGE_CHANNEL_ID and DISCORD_NEWS_CHANNEL_ID in server-side Sites environment settings. Never place the bot token in browser files. Until configured, the site shows Server not connected.

What the Exchange displays

Snapshots refresh every 60 seconds. Current game records include player-sponsored spice harvesting contracts with remaining quota and open/claimed status, plus the standing normal spice sale. Harvest contracts split earnings 15% to the worker and 85% to the sponsor. Buy and sell are supported feed types for future order systems; a general item order book is not currently implemented in the plugin.

The API ignores partial, forged or stale snapshots. Offers older than five minutes are not presented as live. Trades and contract acceptance happen inside Minecraft; the website cannot spend Dunemarks or move cargo.

What News displays

Public Bukkit broadcasts, including Arrakduin sightings, KOOPKRING rotations, Landsraad appointments, invasions and bounties, are forwarded to the news channel. Delayed cross-server Compact notices are added after the proxy plugin-message request is sent. Private player messages and console logs are excluded.

News supports filters, search and paging to older Discord messages. History depends on messages retained in the Discord channel. The reader only accepts messages from the configured DiscordSRV publishing bot.

Connection verification

The bridge and API have automated transport and validation checks. Live DiscordSRV delivery, token permissions and game-server behavior require a connected server and configured channels.
